by: MV2 of Munim, Inc. (made with AI)
description: A labeled corpus of realistic LLM percentile answer blocks, each with the distribution a forecasting harness should extract (or null when the model gave no valid final answer). For each case we record whether two deployed forecasting-bot numeric extractors read, miss, or wrongly accept it. Extractors are transcribed from each tool's published source in numeric_extractors.py and checked offline by test_numeric_formats.py; the live packages are exercised unmodified by compare_extractors.py.

tools.mv2_forecaster: parse_percentiles (v0.1.7). Matches 'Percentile N:' word order only, tolerant of markdown emphasis and an optional '$', keeps indices strictly between 0 and 100, strips thousands commas, allows negatives/scientific notation; returns the {index: value} map only if >= 3 valid percentiles are found, else None.
tools.forecasting_tools: Metaculus forecasting_tools numeric text extractor. A line filter accepts both 'Percentile N' and 'Nth percentile' word orders but is anchored at the line start (a leading '**' or other non-space prefix drops the line); the first number on a line is the level (divided by 100), the second is the value; thousands commas, currency symbols and negatives are handled. Distribution-count validation lives downstream in the library, not in the text extractor, so it is not modeled here.

headline: Neither extractor dominates on numeric answers. mv2-forecaster reads markdown-emphasized percentile blocks and never invents a distribution from reasoning text (0 false positives), but drops the common 'Nth percentile:' word order and anything under 3 points. forecasting-tools reads the 'Nth percentile:' word order, but drops markdown-emphasized blocks and turns a line-anchored base-rate percentile block into a spurious forecast.

cases.note: The canonical 'Percentile N:' block both tools agree on.

A very common way models write percentiles. forecasting-tools' filter accepts the 'Nth percentile' word order; mv2 requires the literal 'Percentile' before the number, so it silently drops the whole block.
Mirror of the ordinal case. mv2's padding class absorbs the '**'; forecasting-tools anchors each line at '^\s*(Percentile|digit)', so a leading '**' drops the line.
Shared strength: both strip thousands separators.
Shared strength: both read signed values and zero (relevant for temperature, net-change, P&L style questions).
Shared strength: mv2 has an optional '$'; forecasting-tools' number regex skips a leading currency symbol.

mv2 requires >= 3 percentiles, so a 2-point answer is dropped. forecasting-tools' text extractor has no such gate (distribution-count checks happen downstream in the library), so its behavior on <3 points is not asserted in this leg.

cases.text:
Looking at base rates for this kind of event:
10th percentile: 2
50th percentile: 5
90th percentile: 11
These are last year's figures; I can't give calibrated percentiles for this year.
cases.note: The model shows a line-anchored historical percentile block, then explicitly declines. forecasting-tools reads the base-rate block as the forecast (false positive); mv2 rejects it because the lines use the 'Nth percentile' word order it does not match. A designed probe, not a frequency estimate.
